title: Synonyms and confusable words 1
about: Near-synonyms that go with different partner words: close a meeting but shut your mouth, a big decision but a large size, finish your homework but end a relationship. Also words meaning 'old' and 'alone' (ancient, antique, elderly, lonely, single, only) and pairs like charge / load, injure / damage and grow / raise.

parts.title: Groups of words with similar meanings
Over to you
parts.note: Завдання з книжки: подивитися в словнику для учнів, з якими словами вживаються big і large. Ось що там знайдеш. Про розмір часто підходять обидва (a big / large city), але large звучить трохи офіційніше й частіше стоїть із number, amount, size. Коли big означає «важливий», «серйозний», «старший» або «багато», його не замінюють на large: a big decision, a big day, a big deal, a big sister, a big eater.

rows: Kharkiv is a big city with lots of parks.
They've bought a large house with a garden.
A large number of people came to the village fair.
Tomorrow's a big day: my sister is getting married.
Sorry I'm late. – Don't worry, it's no big deal.
A warm coat makes a big difference in winter.
My son is a big eater, so I always cook extra.
My big sister taught me to ride a bike.
Her big idea is to open a café by the sea.

items.pattern: close a meeting / discussion / conference
items.meaning: officially end a meeting or a formal event, usually as the person in charge
items.example: At nine o'clock the chair **closed the meeting**, and everyone hurried home.
more: Let's **close the discussion** here and vote next week.
The festival was officially **closed** with fireworks over the river.
items.watchOut: Збори, обговорення, конференцію закривають — close. Shut тут зазвичай не кажуть: це розмовніше слово для дверей, вікон, очей. Можна сказати й end / finish the meeting.

items.pattern: Shut your mouth! · Shut up! (rude) · close your mouth (neutral)
items.meaning: a rude way of telling someone to stop talking; close your mouth is the neutral, polite version
items.example: '**Shut your mouth!**' the man shouted at the referee.
more: My brother told me to **shut my mouth**, and Mum sent him to his room.
**Close your mouth** when you chew, please. Nobody wants to see your food.
items.watchOut: Shut your mouth! і Shut up! — грубі, як «стули пельку». Нейтрально й ввічливо (лікар, батьки дитині) — close your mouth. Загалом shut розмовніше за close: shut / close the door — обидва нормальні.

items.pattern: start the car / engine / motorbike · the car won't start
items.meaning: make a vehicle or its engine begin to work
items.example: Dad **started the engine**, and we set off for the seaside.
more: Lock the doors, **start the car** and let's go!
Our lawnmower is so old that it takes ten minutes to **start**.
items.watchOut: «Завести машину» — start the car, не begin і не launch. З двигунами й транспортом begin не вживають. «Машина не заводиться» — the car won't start.

items.pattern: begin (formal, abstract): how life / the world / the universe began · since time began
items.meaning: came into existence; begin is the usual verb for big, abstract or formal ideas like the beginning of life or the world
items.uk: як виник світ (всесвіт, життя); з початку часів
items.example: My son keeps asking me **how the universe began**.
more: Nobody really knows **how life began**, but there are lots of theories.
People have looked up at the stars and wondered about them **since time began**.
items.watchOut: Begin звучить офіційніше й «книжніше», тож його обирають для великих абстрактних тем. У щоденній розмові start і begin часто однаково природні (The film starts / begins at eight), а от з машинами й двигунами — тільки start.

items.pattern: a big decision · make a big decision · the biggest decision
items.meaning: an important decision that changes a lot
items.example: Choosing a school for your child is a **big decision**.
more: Last year we made a **big decision** and moved to the countryside.
Don't make **big decisions** when you're tired or angry.
items.watchOut: Коли big означає «важливий», його не замінюють на large: a big decision, а не a large decision. Large — про розмір і кількість. «Ухвалити рішення» — make a decision (британці кажуть і take).

items.pattern: a big problem · big problems · not a big problem
items.meaning: a serious problem that is hard to deal with
items.example: Rubbish on the beaches is a **big problem** every summer.
more: Parking isn't a **big problem** in our town.
We had some **big problems** with the builders, but the kitchen is finally finished.
items.watchOut: Про серйозність проблеми кажуть big (або serious, major), зазвичай не large. «Без проблем!» — No problem!

items.pattern: (in) a large size · small / medium / large · a large (= a large size)
items.meaning: the biggest of the usual sizes of clothes, drinks, packets etc.
items.example: The **large size** of this washing powder is much better value.
more: Can I have a **large** popcorn, please?
Sorry, we've sold out of **large sizes** in this jacket.
items.watchOut: Розміри одягу, напоїв, упаковок — small, medium, large, зазвичай не big. «Великий розмір» — a large size; у магазині кажуть і просто a large: Have you got this in a large?

items.pattern: sth ends with sth / with sb doing sth · a happy / sad ending
items.meaning: has something as its last part
items.example: The book **ends with** the two sisters meeting again after forty years.
more: The party **ended with** fireworks over the lake.
Spoiler: the series doesn't have a **happy ending**.
items.watchOut: «Хепі-енд» — a happy ending, а не a happy end. «Фільм закінчується тим, що…» — the film ends with sb doing sth: The film ends with the family going home.

items.pattern: end a relationship / marriage / friendship · end it (with sb)
items.meaning: decide to stop a relationship
items.example: She **ended the relationship** when he forgot her birthday for the third time.
more: It's kinder to **end it** face to face, not by text message.
They **ended their engagement** a month before the wedding.
items.watchOut: Тут end означає «вирішити припинити», тому зазвичай не finish a relationship. «Порвати з кимось» — break up with sb або end it with sb; у британській розмовній ще finish with sb.

items.pattern: finish your homework / an essay / a book / your dinner · finish doing sth
items.meaning: complete something; do the last part of it
items.example: You can go out to play when you've **finished your homework**.
more: I've nearly **finished** the book you lent me.
Have you **finished painting** the bedroom yet?
items.watchOut: Finish — «довести до кінця»; end — «покласти край» або «бути останньою частиною». Тому finish your homework, а не end. Після finish — дієслово з -ing: finish cooking, не finish to cook.

items.pattern: an old friend · old friends · catch up with old friends
items.meaning: someone you have been friends with for a long time (they don't have to be old in years)
items.example: I had lunch with an **old friend** from university on Saturday.
more: Ivan and I are **old friends**: we grew up on the same street.
Christmas is a good time to catch up with **old friends**.
items.watchOut: An old friend — «давній друг», не обов'язково літня людина. Друг похилого віку — an elderly friend. «Колишній друг» — a former friend.

items.pattern: an old building / house / town · a very old building
items.meaning: a building that was built a long time ago
items.example: Our school is in a very **old building** with high ceilings and creaky floors.
more: The town centre is full of **old houses** with tiny windows.
That **old building** by the river is going to be a hotel.
items.watchOut: Про будівлі кажуть old, про дуже давні (тисячі років) — ancient. Не elderly і не antique: elderly — тільки про людей, antique — про цінні старі речі (меблі, прикраси, годинники).

items.pattern: ancient history · study ancient history · That's ancient history! (informal)
items.meaning: the history of very old civilisations like Egypt, Greece and Rome; informally, something from the past that doesn't matter any more
items.uk: історія стародавнього світу; (розм.) справи давно минулих днів
items.example: My daughter loves **ancient history**, especially anything about Egypt.
more: We argued about it years ago, but that's **ancient history** now.
He's doing an evening course in **ancient history** at the local college.
items.watchOut: Ancient вимовляється /ˈeɪnʃənt/ — «ейншент», а не «анциєнт». І не antique history: antique — тільки про цінні старі речі.

items.pattern: in ancient times · ancient Greece / Rome / Egypt
items.meaning: thousands of years ago, in the time of the first civilisations
items.example: **In ancient times**, people used the stars to find their way at sea.
more: The Romans built this road **in ancient times**.
**In ancient times**, salt was so valuable that people sometimes paid with it.
items.watchOut: «У давнину» — in ancient times. А «за старих часів» (не так давно, за життя дідусів) — in the old days; in old times звучить неприродно.

items.pattern: antique furniture / jewellery / clocks · an antique shop · an antique (noun)
items.meaning: old and valuable, usually at least a hundred years old
items.example: My aunt's flat is full of **antique furniture** she bought at auctions.
more: This ring is a piece of **antique jewellery**: it belonged to my great-grandmother.
We found a beautiful **antique clock** in a little shop in Lviv.
items.watchOut: Наголос на другий склад: an-TIQUE /ænˈtiːk/. Antique — про старі цінні речі, не про людей (elderly) і не про давню історію (ancient). Британське написання — jewellery, американське — jewelry.

items.pattern: an elderly person / man / woman · elderly people / parents / relatives · the elderly
items.meaning: a polite word for old, used about people
items.example: Our neighbour does the shopping for an **elderly man** who lives on her floor.
more: My **elderly parents** live with us now.
This flat would be perfect for an **elderly couple**: there are no stairs.
items.watchOut: Elderly — ввічливіше за old, коли йдеться про людей. Про речі так не кажуть: не elderly jewellery, а antique jewellery; не an elderly building, а an old building.

items.pattern: a single parent / mother / father · a single-parent family
items.meaning: a mother or father who brings up a child without a partner
items.example: My mum was a **single parent**, and she worked two jobs to support us.
more: There are lots of **single-parent families** in our building.
Being a **single dad** isn't easy, but I wouldn't change it.
items.watchOut: «Мати-одиначка» — a single mother / parent (в офіційних текстах ще lone parent), а не a lonely mother чи an alone mother. Lonely — «самотній» про почуття, а alone не ставлять перед іменником.

items.pattern: a lonely place / spot / road / beach
items.meaning: a place far from other people, where few people go
items.example: We camped in a **lonely spot** by a lake and didn't see anyone for three days.
more: Few tourists find this **lonely beach** on the north coast.
The old lighthouse stands in a **lonely place** on the cliffs.
items.watchOut: Lonely про місце — «відлюдне, безлюдне», а не «сумне». Про людину lonely — «самотній, якому сумно без інших».

items.pattern: feel / be desperately lonely
items.meaning: extremely lonely and very unhappy about it
items.example: After her divorce, she felt **desperately lonely** in the big empty house.
more: Lots of students feel **desperately lonely** in their first term at university.
He was **desperately lonely** after his dog died.
items.watchOut: «Дуже самотньо» — desperately / terribly / very lonely, але не strongly lonely (калька з «сильно»). Lonely — про почуття: можна жити з людьми й почуватися lonely.

items.pattern: live alone · travel alone · be / feel alone (after a verb, not before a noun)
items.meaning: without other people
items.example: My sister **lives alone** in a tiny flat and loves it.
more: I love **travelling alone**: I can go wherever I want.
Is it safe for a woman to **travel alone** in this country?
items.watchOut: Alone — «сам, без нікого», без смутку; lonely — «самотньо, сумно». Не live lonely, а live alone. Alone не ставлять перед іменником: не an alone woman, а a woman on her own.

items.pattern: a solitary figure / walker · a solitary life
items.meaning: one person on their own, often seen from far away; solitary is rather literary
items.example: Through the fog we could see a **solitary figure** at the top of the hill.
more: A **solitary figure** stood on the bridge in the rain.
My uncle lives a **solitary life** on a small island.
items.watchOut: Solitary — книжне слово: «один-однісінький на тлі порожнього місця». У розмові частіше кажуть on his own або alone. Наголос на перший склад: SOL-i-tary.

items.pattern: the sole survivor (of sth) · the sole owner / reason
items.meaning: the only person (or animal) who stayed alive when all the others died
items.example: A little cat was the **sole survivor** of the house fire.
more: She was the **sole survivor** of the avalanche and later wrote a book about it.
He's the **sole owner** of the business now that his partner has retired.
items.watchOut: Sole = only, але звучить офіційніше, як у новинах: the sole survivor = the only survivor. Вимовляється як soul /səʊl/.

items.pattern: an only child · be an only child · only children
items.meaning: a child who has no brothers or sisters
items.example: As an **only child**, I always wanted a big sister.
more: Our son is an **only child**, so we often invite his cousins to stay.
**Only children** often get on well with adults.
items.watchOut: «Єдина дитина» — an only child, а не a single child і не an alone child. Only тут — прикметник «без братів і сестер», тому потрібен неозначений артикль, а оскільки only починається з голосного звука, це an: an only child.

items.pattern: a unique occasion / opportunity / chance
items.meaning: a special event that will never happen again in the same way
items.example: My grandparents' golden wedding was a **unique occasion**: four generations in one room.
more: The opening of the new bridge was a **unique occasion**: the whole town came to watch.
This trip is a **unique opportunity** to practise the language.
items.watchOut: Unique починається зі звуку /j/, тому a unique, а не an unique. Unique вже означає «єдиний такий», тому very unique багато хто вважає помилкою.

items.pattern: charge your phone / laptop / the battery · be charging
items.meaning: put electricity into a battery
items.example: I forgot to **charge my phone**, and it died halfway through the day.
more: Can I **charge my laptop** here? Is there a socket?
Leave the camera **charging** overnight.
items.watchOut: «Зарядити» телефон чи батарею — charge. А «зарядити» рушницю й «завантажити» машину — load. Не load the battery.

items.pattern: load a van / lorry / ship / the car · load sth into / onto sth · load the dishwasher · load a gun
items.meaning: put goods or a lot of things into a vehicle or machine (also: put bullets into a gun)
items.example: We **loaded the car** with tents and sleeping bags and set off for the mountains.
more: Can you **load the dishwasher** while I clear the table?
The plane can't leave until all the bags are **loaded**.
items.watchOut: «Завантажити машину» — load the car / van, а не charge: charge — тільки про електрику. Обидва варіанти правильні: load the van with boxes = load boxes into the van.

items.pattern: injured people / passengers · be (badly / seriously) injured · injure your knee / back
items.meaning: hurt in an accident or attack (used for people and animals)
items.example: The ski resort has a helicopter for **injured skiers**.
more: He **injured his knee** playing football and can't walk properly.
Two firefighters were **injured** while putting out the fire.
items.watchOut: Про людей і тварин — injured (або hurt), про речі — damaged. «Ніхто не постраждав» — nobody was injured / hurt, а не nobody was damaged.

items.pattern: a damaged sofa / car / roof · damaged goods · be badly damaged
items.meaning: broken or harmed in some way (used for things, not people)
items.example: The delivery men dropped it, so we ended up with a **damaged sofa**.
more: The flood **damaged** hundreds of books in the library.
Our car was **damaged** by hailstones the size of golf balls.
items.watchOut: Damage — про речі: будинок, машину, меблі. Про людей не кажуть damaged, а injured / hurt (хоча про органи кажуть: damage your hearing). Іменник damage незлічуваний: a lot of damage, не damages (damages — компенсація за рішенням суду).

items.pattern: grow crops / plants / vegetables / tomatoes · grow – grew – grown
items.meaning: plant and look after plants so that they develop
items.example: My neighbour **grows vegetables** on his allotment and gives us the extra.
more: I'm trying to **grow plants** on my balcony, but the wind keeps knocking them over.
Farmers in this region **grow crops** like wheat and sunflowers.
items.watchOut: Рослини, овочі, фрукти — grow: grow tomatoes, grow vegetables. Raise crops теж трапляється (частіше в американській), а садівники кажуть raise plants from seed — «вирощувати з насіння», але в щоденній мові про город і сад — grow. Тварин і дітей — raise. Grow children — помилка: дітей raise або bring up.

items.pattern: raise cattle / sheep / animals · raise children / a family
items.meaning: look after animals or children until they are grown
items.example: My uncle **raises sheep** on a farm in the Carpathians.
more: My grandparents **raised five children** on a teacher's salary.
Chickens are easy to **raise** if you have a garden.
items.watchOut: Дітей не «вирощують» — не grow children. Кажуть raise children або bring up children (британці частіше bring up). Про тварин — raise, а також keep або breed.

warmup.uk: Можна тут зарядити телефон? Батарея майже сіла.
warmup.q: Can I ___ my phone here? The battery's almost dead.
warmup.explain: Зарядити телефон чи батарею — charge. Load — завантажити машину або зарядити рушницю.
Мати-одиначка — a single mother. Lonely — самотня (про почуття), а alone не ставлять перед іменником.

warmup.uk: Тато не зміг завести машину, тож ми пішли пішки.
warmup.q: Dad couldn't ___ the car, so we walked.
warmup.explain: Завести машину чи двигун — start. Begin з транспортом не вживають.

warmup.uk: На щастя, в аварії ніхто не постраждав.
warmup.q: Luckily, nobody was ___ in the accident.
warmup.explain: Про людей — injured (або hurt), про речі — damaged.
Рослини й овочі ростуть — grow. Raise — вирощувати (тварин, дітей), йому потрібен додаток; rise — підніматися (ціни, сонце).

warmup.q: This fairy tale has a happy ___.
warmup.explain: Хепі-енд англійською — a happy ending, а не a happy end.

warmup.uk: Мій дідусь живе сам, але йому не самотньо.
warmup.q: My grandad lives ___, but he isn't lonely.
warmup.explain: Alone — сам, без інших людей; lonely — самотньо, сумно. Можна жити alone і не бути lonely.

A.q: The organisers asked the mayor to ___ the conference with a short speech.
A.explain: Конференцію, збори, обговорення закривають — close, не shut.

A.q: Can you wait five minutes? I haven't ___ my coffee yet.
A.explain: Допити, доїсти, доробити — finish. End означає «покласти край», тут не підходить.

A.q: Getting a dog is a ___ decision. Think about it carefully.
A.explain: Коли big означає «важливий», large не підходить: a big decision.

B.q: Many ___ people find online banking difficult.
B.explain: Про людей ввічливо — elderly. Antique — про цінні старі речі, ancient — про давнину.

B.q: Tom has no brothers or sisters. He's ___ child.
B.explain: Єдина дитина в сім'ї — an only child.

B.q: I'm happy to go to the cinema ___. I don't always need company.
B.explain: Alone — сам, без інших людей (і це може бути приємно). Lonely — самотньо, сумно.

C.q: Help me ___ the shopping into the car, please.
C.explain: Завантажити речі в машину — load. Charge — тільки про електрику.

C.q: The fridge was ___ when we moved flats, so the removal company paid for the repair.
C.explain: Про речі — damaged, про людей — injured.

C.q: Is it harder to ___ boys or girls?
C.explain: Дітей і тварин — raise (або bring up про дітей), рослини — grow.

example.title: A summer on Grandad's farm
example.uk:
Минулого літа я гостював у дідуся, який живе сам відтоді, як померла бабуся. Його ферма стоїть у відлюдному місці високо серед пагорбів, але він ніколи не нудьгує: він вирощує овочі й розводить овець.

У суботу ми завантажили фургон сиром і картоплею, щоб везти на ринок, але не змогли завести двигун. Зрештою сусід допоміг нам штовхнути фургон з пагорба, і він завівся.

На ринку дідусь зустрів давнього друга зі школи. Вони сміялися, згадуючи день, коли розбили вчителеві вікно. «Це справи давно минулих днів!» — сказав дідусь.

Того вечора дідусь розповів, що ухвалив важливе рішення: він продасть овець і переїде в квартиру неподалік від нас. Я зрадів, але мені було й трохи сумно.
example.en:
Last summer I stayed with my grandad, who has [[lived alone|b10]] since Grandma died. His farm is in a [[lonely spot|b8]] high in the hills, but he is never bored: he [[grows vegetables|c5]] and [[raises sheep|c6]].

On Saturday we [[loaded the van|c2]] with cheese and potatoes for the market, but we couldn't [[start the engine|a3]]. In the end a neighbour helped us push the van down the hill, and it started.

At the market Grandad met an [[old friend|b1]] from school. They laughed about the day they broke the teacher's window. 'That's [[ancient history|b3]]!' Grandad said.

That evening he told me he had made a [[big decision|a5]]: he was going to sell the sheep and move to a flat near us. I was happy, but a little sad too.
